name: Clast from the Past

pitch_detail.notes: ~100 ft up the basalt band via 7 bolts to a chain anchor on a slab to the right.
~80 ft on 9 bolts; crux pulling a roof near the top.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel from the P2 anchor down roughly 80 ft to the P1 chain anchor.
Rappel from the P1 chain anchor roughly 100 ft to the ground; both raps are within single-rope (60m) range.

rappels: Rappel the route (chain anchors at each pitch)
descent_text: From the P2 anchor, rappel ~80 ft to the P1 chain anchor, then rappel ~100 ft to the ground — both raps are within single-rope (60m) range.
approach: From Randle, WA on US Hwy 12: head south on SR 131, then follow NF-25 for 19.2 miles; just past milepost 21, turn left at the Mosquito Meadows sign onto NF-28 for 2.7 miles; turn left onto NF-77 (rough gravel, drive slowly) for about 2 miles until Pinto Rock comes into view at a large pullout. An evident use trail leads north from the pullout to the base of the formation (~0.3 mi/0.47 km). For North Side, hike around the formation's east side to the base, or summit and rappel the fixed rings to reach the route.
overview: A two-pitch bolted line up the left (west) side of Pinto Rock's north-facing basalt band, with an easy warm-up pitch leading to a harder roof-pull finish.
beta: P1 (5.5) climbs about 100 ft up slabby rock on 7 bolts to a chain anchor; P2 (5.10c/d) continues about 80 ft on 9 bolts through the route's crux, pulling a roof near the top. Rated 5.10b overall. It shares the same lichen-covered basalt band as Sidewinder but follows it up and to the left rather than traversing right.
gear: Quickdraws — the route is fully bolted up the lichen-covered basalt band on Pinto Rock's north face; bring a standard sport rack for the pitch length rather than a trad rack
60m rope — single rope is fine; descent is two rappels down the route from its own chain anchors
Helmet — basalt is knobby and generally solid, but loose blocks and other parties above are a real concern on this face
Alpine quickdraws/slings for rigging the rappels at the chain anchors
fa: Kevin Buselmeier, Jim Yoder & Brenden Sullivan (ground-up first ascent; reported August 2015)
